children: Unstable geopolitics and persistent inflation will weigh on growth in capital markets activity next year, Deutsche Bank analysts write in a report. "The outlook for 2027 is broadly constructive, but risks remain high," says Christian Nolting, the bank's chief investment strategist. Geopolitical tensions won't cool, while high energy prices and trade barriers will result in higher-for-longer inflation, the report's authors say. Interest rates will therefore likely stay stubbornly high, they say. Artificial-intelligence investment will continue, with infrastructure companies a particular beneficiary, but the pace of the AI boom will slow, the strategists say. "AI alone is not enough," Nolting says. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)
